utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, you can have up to one hour and a half, if you require it, to cross-examine this witness.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before I move on to the cross-examination, Mr. May, I would just like to note something that is quite obvious. The last two witnesses were the witnesses whose examination was the slowest since the very beginning, obviously with the intention of using up time, and you could see that for yourself. And for reasons that will become more obvious later --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: No. This is not a proper point. They were witnesses who required some careful examination. This is important evidence. And there was no question of time wasting. If there was, we would have stopped it. Now, let's move on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is why I did object, because you usually object to what I do. We heard questions for ten minutes about the licence plates on the truck, which was so relevant.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Radojkovic, in June 2002, you gave statements to the investigator of the OTP; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: What is your health like now?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: How good was your health at that time, on the 1st and 3rd of June when you gave your statement to the investigators of The Hague Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that when speaking to the working group of the MUP you gave your statement practically from a hospital bed at the medical centre in Kladovo?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in hospital, but in a proper room for that kind of an interview.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Why were you in hospital then?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had some ailments in my chest. My blood pressure was a bit up. That was it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: In the note, it is mentioned that you had had an apoplexy. When did you have an apoplexy, the one you mentioned to the working group?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1985. It was the doctor who mentioned it, not me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And the statement that you gave to the working group was on the 14th of May, 2001; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's when they talked to me, when they interviewed me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Was that one interview or several interviews?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There was one interview in Kladovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Were there any other interviews apart from that one?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A few days later, in the ministry in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So they asked you to come to the ministry in Belgrade to have these other interviews; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I asked for it. I asked to have an interview in Belgrade as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And which were the members of the working group who talked to you on the 14th in Kladovo and which members talked to you in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Kladovo there were three members of the working group. One of them was Captain Karleusa. The other two men, I can't remember their names now, but they're still at the MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, in Belgrade, were they the same interlocutors or did you talk only to one of them?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. All three were there. Perhaps at one point Mr. Karleusa went out. For about ten minutes or so he was absent.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: In that conversation was there a tape recorder there? Was it tape recorded or did they only take notes about the interview with you?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they only took notes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Did you -- when you talked at the medical centre and the physician in charge who gave his approval for you to be heard, was he present or not?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he was not present.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: As mentioned in the Official Note of the working group, on page 5, paragraph 3 of the Official Note, when you speak about the mining of the refrigerator truck, you said: "I finished that and I went to hospital."

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Why did you go to hospital then?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was in 1999, in April. I didn't sleep on the 13th, for three days, and I was exhausted. My biorhythm probably went wrong so I went to see a doctor, a specialist in internal medicine, and he gave me some tranquiliser injections so I could fall asleep.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Who were the doctors who treated you?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The specialist in internal medicine was Dr. Misa - I can't remember his last name now. He's an experienced doctor.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Are they the same doctors who gave their approval to have an interview conducted with you on the premises of the medical centre for you to talk to the members of the working group?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Approval was given by Dr. Rzogic, a specialist neurosurgeon, the one who treated me in 1985 for this minor apoplexy. There was a surgeon, Dr. Mitrovic, and there was Dr. Sinisa, who was director of the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Not at a single point in your statement that you gave to the investigators of this institution here you do not mention that immediately after that event that you say occurred in April 1999 you went to hospital. Why did you not mention that?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When the investigators of the Tribunal at the ministry of Serbia in Belgrade presented the official notes to me that were compiled by the working group on the basis of the interviews that were conducted with me in 2001, I was surprised. I wondered how come they had it, but I realised that that was it. So I didn't really repeat anything from the statement to them. And I said yes, that is the core of the matter. So my statement given to the investigators is very brief because I go by what I said to the working group of the Ministry of the Interior, with just a small reservation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: As for this reservation, I saw that in the note it says in your statement that some of the corpses wore KLA uniforms, and then you corrected that. Is that right? Was it something like that?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Mr. Milosevic. I never stated that in the refrigerator truck there were corpses with KLA uniforms or any other type of uniforms that the KLA used in Kosovo. But a document was presented to me. I think that it was a summary or something, or this was the statement of Mr. Karleusa where he mentioned that in the refrigerator truck there were some KLA uniforms. However, I corrected that. I said no, there were no KLA uniforms. There was a confusion with another case. That is what Mr. Karleusa got wrong.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Oh. So it was Karleusa, not you who said in your statement that there were KLA uniforms, and you corrected that statement, going by what you think that you saw; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Except that I'm not sure whether it's the statement of Mr. Karleusa or whether it's some kind of a report. At any rate, it was mentioned that in the refrigerator truck there were KLA uniforms, and that is not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: If Karleusa did not include this in the report, who could have included it in the report?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know. If I were to see this document where this is mentioned, that there were KLA uniforms there on the corpses in the refrigerator truck, then we would certainly see who wrote that because I really cannot assert anything now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: In your statement to the working group, you say that as for the refrigerator truck that was protruding from the Danube, you found out about it on the 5th of April, 1999, during the NATO aggression; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And then you went to the scene and you saw the truck. The next day when you came, did you see any changes on it or did you see the same thing?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same thing that I saw on the 5th of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that according to the testimony of some people who saw the refrigerator truck fall - and there are about ten of them - they claim that the refrigerator truck fell into the water, and it was a one and a half tonne truck and the one in the picture is five or six tonnes, as far as I can see. Is that story of theirs correct, that there was perhaps a bit of confusion or something like that, something that you could point to? Did anything look suspicious to you when you came there?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't hear these comments. As for this refrigerator truck that I have been referring to, it was a seven and a half tonne truck.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. You gave this set of photographs here that you took.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I gave the negatives.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: But I assume that when the prints were developed, that you recognised them as those that you had taken; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No -- yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction. It was an interpreter's mistake. The witness said, "Yes."

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I have a few questions to put to you. Are they in the same order that you took them in?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know which order you have there in your hands.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: It's the way they've been stapled together. Why don't you look at it yourself.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please have this given to the witness, and I would like them to be placed on the overhead projector so that I could ask him something.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: This is first of the photographs, is it?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The whole set of photographs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let the witness have the set.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Can you compare that to the set you got. I imagine that you did not change the order in your own set. Is that the right order?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: They should be numbered in the top right-hand corner in each case. Are those the photographs, Mr. Radojkovic? Do you recognise them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, those are the photographs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: If you would put them on the overhead projector, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please give me a copy of these photographs. Could you give me a copy of the photographs because I would like to put some questions to Mr. Radojkovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Please look at photograph number 1, for instance. You can see an opening there on the back of the truck, and the door is broken along the right edge. And then on photograph number 2, that can be seen as well. It is closer up, isn't it? Perhaps it's a deformed triangle. That's the best way to put it. Or, for example, like a big arrow head. So it's the entire right side that is ripped; is that right? Please look at photographs number 1 and number 2.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But what has to be disregarded is the reflection of the truck on the water, because the weather was very fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I'm not taking that into account at all. I'm just looking on the -- I'm looking at the right edge of the right door, the very edge of the box that is ripped, and there is a triangular shape that is present on both photographs 1 and 2. As for the other photographs that we will be looking at, for example, photograph 3, then photograph 4 -- I don't know where else it can be seen, the back of the truck. Here. This photograph is number 6135. That's the number. K022. This ripped edge cannot be seen here at all. Look. This is the photograph here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Now, wait a moment. Let the witness deal with it. You're being asked, Mr. Radojkovic, about the rear, and taking photographs 2 and 3, you can see the rip in the rear, and then it's said if you look at photograph number 10 or 9, 8 -- 7, 8, and 9, the rear appears to be different. Now, you gave evidence about this yesterday, but perhaps you would repeat to us how it comes about that there's a rip in the first two photographs but not in the others.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The rip in the truck, the back of the truck, that's photograph number 1, yes. And then photograph number 2, number 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Please show photographs 1 and 2 on the ELMO so that we can see what we're talking about. Number 1 and number 2.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could the witness please speak into the microphone.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This darker part here, is that the rip that you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, that's the rip. That's what he's talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: As far as I can see, that is a rip in the back door by the right edge in the back of the truck. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: On photograph number 2, it can be seen even better.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The closer the truck gets to the bank, the closer up the photographs are.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: The rip can be seen on the right edge of the truck; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, towards the middle.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: The protrusion moves towards the middle then; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Photograph number 2, and then this rip moves along the right-hand side of the truck. Already on the other photographs, no rip can be seen on the right edge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Just a moment. Which photographs are you referring to without the rip?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the very next one, Mr. May. Then take the last one. Take the one but last. Take the one before the one but last. Take a few photographs from the other end and you will see that there's not a rip on a single one of them on the right-hand side of the rear of the truck.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Let's deal with this in an orderly fashion. The photographs being referred to are 8, 9, and 10. Let's put those on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. May, I assume that you have them in front of you. It's so obvious, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I do, but I thought you wanted people to see them. Anyway, they should. Yes, 8, 9 and 10. Now, then, Mr. Radojkovic, would you answer please now the point that I made earlier. You gave an explanation yesterday but would you repeat it so the accused can hear it: How does it come about that there is a rip in the first few photographs but none in the second?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On photographs 8, 9, and 10, there is no writing on the door either. The inscription that was on the truck, that is to say -- Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Don't worry about that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is to say that I took those photographs after I had done some work on the truck. That is to say, when I closed up that rip also, when I pushed in the two legs and arms, and when I closed it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right, Mr. Radojkovic. If you did these photographs -- if you made these photographs after the work you did on the truck, let us disregard them. Let us then look at the first two photographs or, rather, since the first one is somewhat smaller and the other is a close-up, let's look at photograph number 2. Photograph number 2. Could you please put it on the ELMO. This one doesn't work. Sometimes it does work, sometimes it doesn't work. Oh, it works now. So could you please put photograph number 2 now. Can it be seen quite properly and vertically on the right-hand edge of the back of the truck there is a rip and then towards the middle of the right-hand side of the door it is there in the shape of an arrow; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Now, where is that rip on the next photograph, on photograph number 3? On photograph number 3, there is no such rip. It should be here, here where you're holding the pointer, as far as I can see. On that side. On that side, on the previous photograph, there is a rip. On this side on this photograph, it's quite different. It's a completely regularly shaped rip. Oh, this went off on my monitor. Oh, all right. So are you sure it's the same truck?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, Mr. Milosevic, quite sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: How do you then explain this kind of difference in terms of the place where the rip is and also in the shape of the rip between photographs 2 and 3?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I explained that yesterday. While the truck was being pulled out of the water, Zivadin Djordjevic, a diver, was in the water all the time. He wore his diving outfit. He was trying to get the wheels straight. He was doing his best in order to pull the truck out. He informed me that there was something that was protruding out of the truck, and since I was wearing normal clothes - I mean, I had gone to work - it was very deep there so I could not get in. But as the truck was getting out, I mean he kept trying to close this as much as he could. Secondly, what you can see here on photograph 3, on the upper part, this sort of flat thing, that is part of the back of the door. There is -- there is some kind of wood there on the back of the door.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Let's not waste any time, Mr. Radojkovic. I'm not asking you about diver's outfits or any such thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: No. But you have raised a point about this rip and the witness must be able to finish his explanation about it. Now, is there anything more you wanted to say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm a bit embarrassed that this is being brought into question now. I would kindly ask the Court to ask the Ministry of the Interior in Belgrade for the original of the negative. They have it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Don't be embarrassed. No need at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Radojkovic, you earlier said that the picture number 3 was taken before you did something on the truck. Please take a look at number 9. Could you take a look at picture number 9. Do you think the image, number 3 and number 9, look similar? Which is suggested. Picture number 3 was taken after you did some repair job on the truck; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. Number 3 was certainly not taken before this opening was closed. After all, the negative would show everything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, please go on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just to say that it's open to the Prosecution to provide any evidence that it wishes in rebuttal in relation to this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We've got no interpretation.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters did not hear anything until right now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, the interpreters didn't hear what you said. But if it was argument about this point, let's try and move on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. May, what I was saying was that I'm using materials that you presented -- or, rather, that the other side presented. These are these photographs. And I believe it is quite logical for me to ask for an explanation of an obvious difference in the damage on the back side of the truck that can be seen in photographs 2 and 3 respectively. You believe that the witness did answer these questions, and now I have further questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Radojkovic, on this photograph number 3, can it be seen that you had already removed the chain and padlock and that the refrigerator truck was practically open; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Photograph 3 does not show that. The chain and the padlock are still there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Please, where are the chain and padlock on photograph number 3?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if we're looking at the same photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: It's the third one. It's this one up here.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes here. In the upper part, at the end of the white thing. Here it is, the chain and the padlock. It's a thin chain. It is thinner than my small finger. See, up here. That is where the chain is and the padlock. On the original photographs, this can be seen a bit better, because the padlock happened to be turned to the back side so you could really see it quite properly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: If you look at the next photograph, 4, you have it more clearly. Is that it?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Tell me, please, was it on the first day that you opened this with an instrument?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not on the first day. On the 5th of April it was noticed, and the 6th of April it was removed -- moved out to such a distance that we could open it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Did you continue making photographs then? You said you made a part of the photographs on the 5th and a part on the 6th.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right. Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Now, give me answer to a very important question. How come that when you opened this refrigerator lorry and saw the bodies, here in your statement, it says: "It is my job to investigate crime scenes, to establish what happened. It was my job also to secure potential evidence and investigate all kinds of crimes starting with burglaries and up to murders. I was also trained as a police scene-of-crime photographer. That is also my responsibility." So you are a qualified crime investigation inspector, photograph, and so on. You opened the door. How come you didn't make a single photograph of the corpses inside?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I opened the door. It is two doors, actually, a double door. There were 30 people operating the cranes around me. There were some people near the village of Tekija who were, it is true, at a certain distance on the road and near the edge of the woods. So I thought they could see it. I opened the door and immediately closed it. It didn't matter, because the corpses weren't going anywhere. I could come back in an hour or two and open the door again.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Please. Yesterday when you said you returned on the second day - and I believe it was Judge Kwon who asked you, but I'm not sure - what time it was, you said between 12 and 1300 or perhaps a little later. Between 12 and 1300 hours is a very good time for taking photographs. As you said you could do it in an hour or two, why didn't you? I assume that you were able to photograph the bodies that you had found inside.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was able, but the investigating judge had to come, the public prosecutor had to come. By that time, I just informed them of the contents. And the investigating judge said he didn't even want to look; it was in the jurisdiction of the District Court. So I went to see my boss and tell him what had been found in the refrigerator lorry. It is a big job. It surpasses my abilities or the abilities of the police station where I work.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Radojkovic, you are a qualified police inspector, and you know very well that evidence has to be collected from the scene of the crime immediately, without delay. The scene of the crime is photographed immediately, and all the clues are gathered without delay. How come you didn't make a single photograph of the bodies?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will explain, Mr. Milosevic. When Tomislav Milojkovic, president of the District Court in Kladovo at the time, the investigating judge, stated that it was not within his competence, the district public prosecutor was invited to come from Negotin, and it was agreed that the public prosecutor from Negotin and the investigating judge should come, and once they come and gave me orders to take photographs, I would have done it, but I didn't get such instructions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So are you saying that until the investigating judge comes, the scene-of-crime officers are not allowed to take photographs of the scene and collect evidence that would later help establish facts? You are not going to tell me that without the permission of the investigating judge you cannot photograph the place.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Under the law on criminal procedure that applied at the moment, the police was able to do that. According to the new law, they can't even do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You have been an inspector for a long time, for many years. You had a camera with you. You made pictures of the refrigerator lorry. The point of this whole story are the corpses, and we can't see the corpses anywhere. How is that possible? How is it possible that you didn't make a single photograph of the corpses?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't. There aren't any.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: He has answered that now twice, so there's no need to repeat the question. And of course there is a photograph showing a foot.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right, Mr. May. I really cannot understand this. Yesterday, it wasn't clear even to you until we clarified in my cross-examination of Mr. Karleusa that those corpses have not been even exhumed or found, nor does anybody know where they are at all, because he came to testify about the refrigerator lorry, and instead he testified to the exhumation of bodies in Batajnica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: If you want to put to the witness - and if it's your case you should - that there weren't corpses in the truck, then you should put it to him so he can deal with it, if that is your case.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know what happened. I'm just trying to establish how it is possible that the competent police officer who arrives at the scene, finds corpses there, and it is one of his duties, among others, to make photographs of the refrigerator lorry from the side, from the front --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: You have made that point several times. He has given his answer. It will be a matter for the Court to consider in due course. There's no point going over it again.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right, Mr. May.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Is it the usual practice, Mr. Radojkovic, when you go out to the scene of the crime to immediately make photographs of whatever you find there?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and that's precisely what I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Except for the main thing, the corpses; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. All right, Mr. Radojkovic. Do you know anything about the following: These corpses that you found there have not yet been exhumed, identified, found anywhere. Are you aware of that as a police officer?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I know that they have not been found, located yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You said yesterday during examination-in-chief - and we will perhaps come back to that later - that the death of these persons, and you spoke as a man with experience, which I believe you are, occurred two or three days before you found them; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was my assumption.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Now, if death had occurred two or three days before you found them in the Danube, do you have any idea for how long they might have been in the Danube? Was it one day in the water, a day and a half, for instance?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Judging by the changes on the skin of the fingers and toes, they had not been in the water for more than a day and a half or two.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Two days?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A day and a half at the most.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. A day and a half or two. And they were killed two or three days before you found them.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's my opinion.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: If we subtract this one day and a half before -- from this two and a half days or three, they were killed shortly -- a day before.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, unless they were frozen in the refrigerator lorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: We'll deal with that. If death occurred two or three days before they were discovered, is it possible or probable -- and I'm asking you as a crime investigation inspector, is it possible that in that short period of time they could have been killed, buried, exhumed, and then transported by that refrigerator lorry to the Danube? Is it possible that they had already been buried and then dug out?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't think they had been buried at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You said at one point that the truck was taken to Petrovo Selo and a grave in Petrovo Selo was also mentioned. And I read in this press release that was mentioned when Karleusa was cross-examined that these graves might date back to 1945 or 1955. Did I conclude correctly that the lorry was taken to Petrovo Selo empty?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. An empty lorry was taken on a flatbed truck to Petrovo Selo.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. I'm interested in one little detail. At first glance, it is a very minor detail. I beg your pardon, I can't locate this in my papers. It must be in this note. You speak, and you spoke yesterday, about blowing up the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. refrigerator lorry using industrial explosives; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And here a term is used which nobody uses where we come from, and namely that is "explosives for production." Have you yourself ever used this term "explosives for production"?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not familiar with the term.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: It's not familiar to you. Well, it's not familiar to me either. In our country, we say "industrial explosives," explosives used in the economy as opposed to those used in mines, quarries, et cetera, but there are no explosives for production.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am pointing this out, Mr. May, because I believe that this was originally written in English and then translated into Serbian, because no native speaker of Serbian would ever say "explosives for production." And even the man who was quoted here believes this to be a very odd term, "explosives for production," "manufacturing explosives." And he gave his statement in Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Isn't that true, Mr. Radojkovic?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The interview was conducted in the Serbian language.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I thought that much. I just wanted to make it plain. Because as far as this testimony and their engineering is concerned - no offence meant to you - there are many odd things. However, let's move on. You invited a diver to come. I won't dwell on that. And now let's come back to the issue of the photographs. You gave the explanation you gave, but please explain -- okay. You didn't make certain photographs, although you said yourself that they should be made immediately at the scene of the crime, but did you also draft a dispatch and send it to the competent secretariat of the MUP in Bor, which is also your responsibility?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 5th of April, 1999, in the evening, I visited the scene of the crime together with Nenad Popovic, crime investigation technician.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Was it on the first day?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was the first day. I don't know whether a dispatch had been sent to the Bor SUP. I didn't send any. On the next day, however, the 6th of April, when the refrigerator lorry had already been opened, I personally wrote a dispatch to the Bor SUP. I signed it together with my -- and my boss signed it, Milan Stevanovic. Police stations at that time were dispersed around the secretariat. It was a very unpleasant dispatch, written in elliptical terms to the SUP of Bor because there was a war going on, and basically I invited them to get involved.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right, but did you make a report on your on-site investigation?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. On the 5th of April, as you have said yourself, you have already completed some investigative work: You established that there was a lorry in the water, you established the type of truck, the damage on it. Was it your duty also to make a report, a record of your findings? Why is there no such record?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether the record was drawn up. The operative employee was supposed to do that, Mr. Popovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Wasn't it your duty to make note of all the findings that you had by that time; that there was a lorry in the water, the type, the damage, et cetera? You had a diver there who had already completed certain work; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: But you didn't make a record. Why?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I, as a crime investigations technician, do not make records.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. But do you go out to investigate scenes of crimes without an inspector?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Why did you do so this time?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because the lorry was at a 30-metre distance in the water, 30 metres away from the bank, and we had just gone there with the idea of seeing whether it was there at all and what it was. All you could see was the tip of this trailer box. You can't see much. The depth of the water at that place is 12 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. You photographed the lorry except the time when it was in the water, only when it was pulled out with all of its four wheels.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think it is among these photographs, but I do have one photograph taken on the 5th where you could see it. I believe it is on the negative.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: But it's not here?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's not here. I believe it exists on this negative that I have kept. There is one photograph where you can only see this trailer box and this dirty strip on the upper corner from the dirt in the water.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You spoke about that yesterday, about this dirty strip. You can see it on this first photograph. How do you explain that these dirty strips are missing on the rear side of the box? Because a chassis is a 3D thing. You can't have a dirty strip on one side and not the other, if that is indeed what you are trying to explain. Where it ends on one side, it should continue on the other side, depending on the position of the truck, but I suppose it should be visible too.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, the right side of the truck, of every truck, is always cleaner. The lateral sides are always cleaner than the rear and even than the front, because the wheels always spray dirt and mud and stuff. So on the lateral side, you can clearly see this dirt strip, this mark made by the water.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, it doesn't make sense to me, and that's why I'm asking all these questions. Could you please tell me, you say two human feet were protruding from the lorry and nobody noticed it except you.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Who else noticed them?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Djordjevic, the diver, noticed it before I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: But I mean except for you and the diver.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, there were 20 of us there. We were trying to conceal it somehow so that not everybody sees it. I was there with Nenad Popovic, Momcilo Sujranovic, all of my colleagues. People from the hydroelectric power plant saw it. There is one photograph, and I don't know, Your Honours, if you have it. You can see people standing around the truck.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I want to ask you one more thing. You tried to explain in your statement that nobody saw it. Everybody backed off to a certain distance, and I do see people on one of the photographs, so they must have seen it. I don't know which number this photograph is, but you can see at least two men standing here except for you who were taking the photo.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Milosevic. But when I said I told the people to back away, not to see the bodies in the truck, it was not the only reason. It was realistic to expect that there were explosives laid in the truck. Why should we all get killed if I had to?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I understand your care for your men. That's very kind on your part and nobody questions your professional care for your underlings. But I understood from what you were saying a moment ago that you wanted to conceal this at any cost. Why? For what reason? In your normal practice when you investigate crime scenes, is it a rule to cover up whatever you are doing, apart from providing normal security around the scene of the crime so that nothing can be touched and tampered with? Why were you trying to conceal anything on this occasion?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was very unpleasant, embarrassing as a job to pull out this truck. And the job was a very time-consuming one. With those feet and arm protruding all the time, there were a lot of machinery operators, employees, workers who had to do this work in the vicinity of the truck all the time and watch this all the time, these feet and arm. So I don't see anything unusual about the fact that we first closed the door and then continued pulling it out. There was no ill intention involved. It was just out of respect for those people. How could you come close to that truck to handle it while -- and attach a cable while a human arm or foot is protruding all the time?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: It is your job to conduct the investigation on this site. It is -- I understand that you didn't want your men traumatised. I understand that was your motivation. But that's not your job. Your job was to make photographs. You are paid to be exposed to such traumatic experience.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We have been over this matter now, particularly the photographs.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. All right, Mr. May.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Please tell me, as an eyewitness and an experienced crime investigation technician, how did you assess the cause of this damage on the truck? Because we didn't really understand each other on this point. How come there is a difference between what is depicted on various photographs?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We've also been over this point. Unless you've got a new question, Mr. Milosevic, we're not going to return to it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me now, you say you closed this damaged part with nuts and bolts; is that right? Screws.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was screws. And Zivadin Djordjevic gave them to me from his bag.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: How long did you keep the door open?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Three or four seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So your entire perception took place during those three or four seconds while you kept the door open?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I climbed up to the box and I looked inside. I think that the door was not wide open either. I think only the right side of the door was open a bit so that I could go in.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Already on that day, on the 6th, that is - that is the second day - if I understood you correctly, there was a crime inspector with you there on the second day.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, since the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And did you and he compile a report on what you had seen and found?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Only a telegram was sent to the SUP Bor.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So it was known then to you, or rather, you knew what was in the truck. You opened the door, you saw it. You, the crime inspector, and you did not record this at all. You did not write a report.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know how to answer this question: Why did you not do that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: He has already explained; it wasn't his job.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. May, perhaps you haven't noticed. I asked him whether a crime inspector was with him at the time, and he says that that is his job, the crime inspector's job. So I'm asking him whether the two of them compiled a report then, and he says they did not.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I answer this question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A crime policeman was with me, Nenad Popovic. We saw that. We returned to the police station, and we presented this to the head of the SUP and the head of the department, what we found and what was in this refrigerator truck. In practice, we never actually made reports on the site itself. We don't have the right kind of equipment for doing that. As for the situation on the scene itself, it can be described in a report a day or two or three days later. But all of this would move under the jurisdiction of the District Court in Negotin, and it is the investigating judge who compiles this kind of report. We could only compile an Official Note which we would then present to the investigating judge. Since Negotin is 60 kilometres away from Kladovo, nothing was written except for this telegram that I wrote, my superior -- supervisor signed it, and we sent it to the SUP Bor.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. But in that statement of yours, you say that this man of yours in Kladovo, right, your boss --

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: -- said that this had to be concealed. Did you ask him why?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the evening, at a small meeting of the local police where I was, Nenad Popovic, Milan Stevanovic, Vukasin Sperlic, the head, perhaps somebody else was there as well, the objective was not to conceal it. We were in favour of the following solution: This inscription on the truck that was on the right-hand side that said Progres Export Slaughterhouse Prizren, that we hide that so that it would not attract the attention of the workers who were trying to get the truck out of the Danube; secondly, so that the Romanians would not be observing us perhaps from their military ships that were there in a bay towards Osava [phoen]. I mean, I don't know, they were about a kilometre away from us, they could notice this easily, but they were going all around and they could think all sorts of things.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You spoke about that yesterday, so I don't want to dwell on that. The next day, the 7th of April, in the statement that was compiled by the working group, you went to the scene again and you saw a truck full of coffins and also an undertaker's vehicle.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I saw it on the road, on the road. That this came from Kladovo. A truck from -- a truck with coffins and also an undertaker's vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I do not see the link between the two, that's why I'm asking you. Because you say that these corpses were taken somewhere. They were not taken in coffins, as far as I understood.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: What happened to these coffins? What's this all about? I simply cannot link that part of your statement to the other part where you say that they were driven away in a truck or something.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understand your question. A truck was sent from Kladovo, from the public utility enterprise there, with a certain number of coffins. I don't know exactly how many. And there was also an undertaker's vehicle. I saw this, and I knew immediately that that's not the way this can be Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. done. This was already around 11.00 or 12.00. I knew that actually SUP Bor did not know anything about this then, because I wondered myself, What are we going to do with these coffins? First of all, all of Kladovo and Negotin, I think, cannot collect 80 coffins in one day.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I don't understand. Did you say ten?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said 80. Then the truck with the coffins went back, because we did not even have radio communication with the police in Kladovo from the site itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I understand. So you returned the truck because you thought that that was not the right way to resolve this. Did I understand you properly?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Four or five coffins could not resolve this situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. And then here it says in this note -- I don't know. What is yours and what is -- now, look. It says here Bosko, and I imagine that's you; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: On page 6 of this Official Note, it says: "Bosko has information that on a certain day, about 2200 hours until 2230 hours, people who were coming back from the funeral, as they were moving along the road towards Tekija or the tunnel from Golubinje Kazan noticed two jeeps and men in uniforms, in camouflage uniforms. When they were passing by, the people in camouflage uniforms jumped into the ditch in order to hide. They noticed that the people in uniform were looking in the direction of the Danube, most probably at the refrigerator truck that was floating towards -- the refrigerator truck that was probably thrown before the second tunnel in the direction of Kladovo." Could you explain this to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, in the brief statement that I gave to the investigators of The Hague Tribunal, I said and I asked that this Official Note that you also have and that the Court has and that the Prosecutor has, that I fully support it until that part, because that is what I did with my own hands and that is what I saw with my own eyes. As for the second part, I said that I did not give this to the Tribunal. I never would give this to the Tribunal. I gave it to the working group, as to my colleagues, and that can be used only for further investigations in the police, not the Tribunal. And nobody in the Tribunal asked me about this here either. There's no need for that. So this is just talk.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Radojkovic, you're being asked about it now, and one way or another, the information is before us. Now, can you help us about this, as to any information you may have had about how the truck got into the water?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Everything that is written in that statement is what I heard, but none of it was checked. It's not for me to check. It is for me to notify others and then they will check what is relevant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: No, of course, we understand that. It's not for you to check. But this is what you heard, is it, what's in this note?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Radojkovic, I am asking you -- I mean, I want this to be clear to you. I'm asking you about this because I did not get this from you. I did not get this from the working group. I got it from this false prosecution. They are the ones who are abusing this. So I would like to clear this up with you to see what the truth is and what is not the truth. Because it is amazing to me that somebody is coming back from a funeral at 10.00 p.m. Please, who is buried at night in our part of the world? Where did you get that kind of information? "Bosko has this information," et cetera. You heard from someone that someone had seen that. You did not see it yourself.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I am -- that's what I'm saying. I don't even know how the Tribunal got this. I never would have given this to the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: But it's not -- it's something that you saw, that's what matters to me. So this was just hearsay. You told those people at the SUP what you heard from someone else.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Right. That is what I want to clarify. Look at another example, another example on the very same page of that note.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I read it. I know all of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I want to read it to you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters note that they cannot follow this speed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Now, I'm stopping you. You're going too quickly for the interpreters. If you're going to read out, remember to read slowly.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right, Mr. May. I'm going to read slowly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: On page 5 of this so-called phantom note, phantom Official Note that nobody signed, it says: "Petrovic Zivojin saw something, a security guard. He saw something." It doesn't matter. He worked and then he conveyed this to Ljubo, a driver in Tekija, and then Ljubo Maksimovic told Bosko Radojkovic about this. Please. This is not hearsay. This is a third degree hearsay. One person sees something, then he tells a driver about it, and then this driver tells a third person, and then this person tells Radojkovic. Please, I'm asking you, Mr. Radojkovic, is this a serious thing? Can -- can this kind of allegation be based on such hearsay?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, I told my colleagues in the MUP what I really heard, and I really think that it is not proper for it to be in the Tribunal now because this is not verified facts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know who gave this here?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't know. I first saw this when I saw the investigator.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, your minister, Dusan Mihajlovic, all this hearsay here. I'm not the one who gave it to them, that's for sure, and it's not you either, from what I can see.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it wasn't me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: This is just a mistake. Never mind. It says Gornji Milanovac. It is obvious that it was written by somebody who did not live in that area. Because in that area, nobody even says "Donji Milanovac," they just say "Milanovac" and half the people don't even know that a Gornji Milanovac exists; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I noticed that mistake too, but that's not for me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: It's not for you. I am just indicating things that are quite clear to me, bearing in mind the fact that I know that area, like all of Serbia, very well but that part in particular, that nobody from there could put it that way. And that could not be your statement, because you are from there. Look at what it says here: "Rumour has it that before this case --" Please. This in is an Official Note that describes the interview with Bosko Radojkovic. No one else; Bosko Radojkovic. "Rumour has it," et cetera, et cetera. That's what it says here. Now, please, I don't know whether I'll be able to find it in here straight away. Let me find it. You informed your chief of police -- here it is. That is page 4. "I informed him about the existence of 30 corpses." So I imagine that when you were telling your chief of police how many corpses there were, you were giving them -- him your assessment, that there were 30 corpses. How did later on -- how did it turn out later on that there were 50 or 56 or 58 or whatever? Can you explain this to me?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I'll try. When I opened the door, the corpses were up to the door itself, and then there was a bigger, bigger pile towards the middle of the box and then deep inside there were less of them. When I looked in, I saw just one pile of corpses, and of course since - how should I put this? - this is sort of like a small pile, a small stack, I was not sure whether the corpses went all the way to the end of the refrigerator truck. But superficially, on the basis of what I could see in a few seconds --

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Let's not waste any time. That was your assessment and that is what you told your chief of police.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To be quite frank, my assessment was that there were even more of them, but I didn't dare include that in the note.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. I am really interested in one thing: The reservists of the DB were present, the state security. I have been -- I was there for a long time, and I never heard of DB reservists. Could you have said something as nonsensical as that, that there were DB reservists, state security reservists there?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: That's what the note about your statement contains. And who knows what else others would say, others whose statements are being tendered here into evidence where -- and now you have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Milosevic. Yes. Ask a question.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll be brief, Mr. May.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Please. Did you say that the same night, at fifteen past one a.m., four men in camouflage uniforms came in jeeps to Djerdap, et cetera, et cetera? Did you state that?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I stated that, that I had heard that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: That you had heard that?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that I heard that. That's precisely what it says. That is this other part of the statement that I expressed my reservations about to the investigators at The Hague Tribunal, because it is something that I heard about.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: It's the customs officer who heard about this and he told his friend and this friend told you?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And you included that in an Official Note?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Radojkovic, do you think that if somebody hears a rumour, perhaps it may prove to be true, but does the police then try to find out what the actual facts are? The investigating judge, does he try to find out what the actual facts are or is everything just taken for granted?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, as a policeman, I am duty bound in respect of everything that I hear from other citizens. Whether it's a crime or any other event, it is my duty to inform my service about that. If I do not do this, that means that I commit at least a disciplinary infraction. So then people work from this kind of information. And a service that may be interested in will then further check the information that I provided.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You say that you held the door open briefly and that you saw a pile of corpses. Did you come to any conclusion as to who these people were, where they came from, how they were killed, where they were killed, except for what you assessed, that they were not dead for more than two or three days, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this respect, I could only notice the external injuries they had, those that were visible to the naked eye. I noticed how they were dressed. But where these people were from, that is something that could not be concluded on the basis of anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that General Djordjevic ordered an autopsy to be carried out and that it was impossible to carry it out because of some reasons there, because it was not possible to do it in Kladovo or whatever?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Throughout the proceedings, I was near the Danube, by the Danube. I was on the bank of the Danube. And those people who talked to somebody else, using phones, whatever, they were about two kilometres away from me, at the border crossing in Tekija. So I did not hear any of that. Of course, I could assume that possibly these corpses would be transported to Belgrade and that then the exhumation -- no, rather, the autopsy would be carried out, because we really did not have the manpower or the equipment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Please tell me, because there are many things here that are really -- I mean questions. How come this -- how come this mention of the Kurds? Who launched this idea concerning the Kurds?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since this attracted a lot of attention in Tekija and in Kladovo, people started talking about it a lot. This is right by the road between Kladovo and Belgrade. People go to work, many people saw this, and then people were wondering what to do with this? And then we sort of thought, well, let's invent a story. Let's say that perhaps they were Kurds or some kind of asylum seekers who were trying to flee from Yugoslavia because of the war, because the bombing, that they were trying to flee to Romania, because there was a case like that, a true case with Kurds, with asylum seekers nearby in Golubovac. So we thought that we could use a similar kind of story.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I am not bringing into question anything in relation to you now. Yesterday when Karleusa was testifying, I presented official information of the State Security Service here and also the Official Note of the public prosecutor of the municipality, the -- in connection with the criminal group that was led by the brother of the owner of this crime review newspaper. And it also includes some members of the police. Do you know anything about this local group of criminals? Let me just add one more thing; it's not only that they smuggled cigarettes, weapons, et cetera, but they also transported people across the Danube and then they also charged 500 German marks per person. Do you know anything about this?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that there were asylum seekers and that people were being transported, but who does this, I really don't know. Secondly, Mr. Vitomirovic is in Zajecar, and that's pretty far away. We are functionally related to Bor, to the Bor district. So we have less communication with Zajecar. I am not aware of that, whether these persons took part in that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You don't know? You don't know about the village of Sipikovo towards Vidin and all that, these transports? You call that the transport of asylum seekers; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know how to put this. From Afghanistan, from Iran, from the Sudan, from Nigeria, I encounter these people. I don't know whether they are asylum seekers or immigrants or whatever.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Never mind. It doesn't matter what we're going to call them. You Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. said Sudan, Afghanistan, Nigeria, et cetera. It doesn't matter. Who is organising this operation?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know. Secondly, as for Sipikovo, I've just heard about it. I know that it's somewhere towards the Bulgarian border. The municipality of Kladovo borders Romania only.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Kladovo is on the border that is actually the Danube. I don't want to go beyond your area, but that's quite clear. Doesn't it seem to you, Mr. Radojkovic, in view of the fact that you know yourself not only about Zajecar but also about your own area, about this smuggling of people from different countries that you mentioned and so on, every piece of dirt that is committed by these gangs, these criminal gangs, should all that be ascribed to the police that were defending the country during the war?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not say that I knew who the intermediary was in the smuggling of these asylum seekers, I said that I knew that there were asylum seekers.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Radojkovic, I am not asking you here. I mean, this is not a hearing about who these people are. You know that this is a phenomenon that does exist in that area where the state border is and that is no rarity at that section of the state border.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Now, since you said that it was only the second time that you talked to the working group that there were 86 bodies in the truck and they all had head injuries inflicted by various instruments and that only one body, a boy aged 18 to 20 - and yesterday you said from 17 to 20, never mind - so a young man, he had an entry/exit wound. So nobody had been killed by firearms. All of them were killed in some different way. Now, my question is the following as related to such a claim with regard to these 86 bodies, and also it should be seen that there are wounds in the chest. A layman can see an entry/exit wound. But for this kind of claim as to the cause of death, I assume that you will agree that this would have to involve a detailed examination of the bodies; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My assertion yesterday was not the way you are putting it now. What I stated yesterday was that this young man, who was about 17, 18, 20, he did have an entry/exit wound.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I'm not questioning that you stated that.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just said that I saw him and that I'm making an assertion about him because he was naked and you could see the chest wound properly. As for the others, who were dressed, I did not look, because how could I as they were being dragged? They could only, what, fall in? I said that I only saw that he had an entry/exit wound. None of the others, I didn't claim anything about the others. I only said what I saw. I saw that he had an entry/exit wound.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Did I read that somewhere or did it seem to me -- I don't want to look through this note again -- that you actually said that for the most part, they were killed by some instruments that they had been hit with?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I stated.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So apart from opening the door of the refrigerator truck and taking part in the transport of the bodies, objectively speaking, you had no other contact with these bodies. You did not examine them in any way.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree with that statement, Mr. Milosevic. Yesterday I said and I can say only now what I saw with my very own eyes. In order to note certain injuries, it is sufficient to cast a glance. You don't really need an examination. I can tell you that I saw, during my regular work, murders committed by an axe. I saw slaughtered corpses. I saw corpses with slit throats not related to this in any way. I have seen violent deaths along a broad spectrum, and I know how injuries are sustained. I know what I can assume. So as for what I saw in the refrigerator truck, I was in a position to say, "Well, this could have been the result of that." The statement I gave to the working group of the ministry had only one objective in the description of these corpses; when they get to these corpses, when they exhume them, because they were probably buried later, so that on the basis of these wounds and on the basis of this clothing, they could say, "Right, those are the bodies that were taken out of the refrigerator truck." Because I said that even my boots are in that truck, the ones that I threw after I finished this. And also red gloves that I had on my hands. So that this would be a trace, this would be a lead so that they could recognise this. So the description I gave to the working group of the MUP had only that objective. How all of this reached the Tribunal, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: That's not the question that is being raised here anyway. As an experienced policeman, when the bodies were being transported from the refrigerator truck to other vehicles, did you try to check the clothing and to ascertain the identity at least of some of these persons?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In case of a few men, when time allowed me, I put my hand into their pockets or whatever, and I didn't find anything. In the case of a little girl, the corpse of a little girl who was about 7 or 8 years old, she had a rucksack, a little bag.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: What did she have?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: She had a little bag, a little rucksack or whatever. Momcilo Sujranovic, Nenad Popovic, my colleagues who were with me, we were looking at this little girl together. We opened the bag. The two of us opened this bag. She had a UNICEF notebook, A4 format, and in that bag were some colour crayons and a little doll. And in the notebook, there was only the drawing of a house and some little flowers, nothing else. We opened that in order to see what this was and who these people were. No documents were found on the corpses.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I think it's enough about this phantom refrigerator lorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, you've got four minutes left.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. May. I think there is no need for me to cross-examine this witness about all the parts of his statement which he describes himself as not factual but derived from hearsay and rumours, and they abound in this case, as you can see.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you one more thing about this. You set the refrigerator lorry on fire; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And after that, you blew it up.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You did that on your own initiative or was it somebody who told you to do it?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the head of the Bor SUP who told us to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So the only thing that was your initiative was this story about the Kurds. The rest you didn't do of your own accord.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't really an initiative. It was just conversation. We were just thinking aloud how to present some sort of story to the public. There were various versions, and then somebody said, "Well, let's plant a story, say it was the Kurds or something." And I said yes, that would make things easier.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: We discussed this working group and this article written by Vitomirovic. And this Ilija Matic, head of state security, you heard about him?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Both of them are members of this new party, New Democracy, headed by Dusan Mihajlovic.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You don't know about that?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And both of them are members of this criminal group that I mentioned yesterday?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No further questions, Mr. May.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Kay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: No questions. Mr. Ryneveld, it is time for the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Your Honours, I will have just a few questions. Do you want me to do it before the break or after the break? But there are four very brief areas that I need to re-examine upon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Perhaps you could do it before the break, if they're brief.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Fine. I'll do it very quickly

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: First of all, sir, the photographs that you were shown --

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Could the witness be shown, please, photographs 2 and 3 in the set of ten.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: First of all, sir, as a professional photographer, would you agree that camera angles make a difference with respect to what can be seen?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And also the progress of pulling out the truck. The nearer it comes to the bank of the river, the resistance of the water increases, because the dragging accelerates and the water resistance pushes the rear side towards the interior. The damage on the door resulted from the force which acted from inside towards the exterior. The pressure of the bodies, in other words, resulted in this damage. The slit increased. It is quite normal for these plywood doors to return to their original position, at least to some extent, once the whole vehicle is removed from the water.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: One final question on the flap or the hole, as it were.
